newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Transaero promotes Pleshakov to chairman.
newsitem.headline: Transaero promotes Pleshakov to chairman.

text.p: The shareholders of Russian private airline Transaero last week promoted chief executive Alexander Pleshakov to the vacant post of chairman, a company spokeswoman said on Thursday.
Natalya Alexashina, giving the first news of the appointment, said Pleshakov was elected on June 11. First deputy chief excecutive Nikolai Kozhevnikov had replaced him as chief executive.

In 1991, Pleshakov, 33, was one of the founders of Transaero, which has been one of the most successful new airlines in Russia, becoming the country's largest private carrier with 14 Western passenger jets, 13 of which are leased.
State-controlled Aeroflot International Airlines, Russia's biggest carrier, owns five percent of Transaero.

Pleshakov's mother is Tatyana Anodina, head of the CIS Aviation Committee, an inter-state agency which controls air carriers in Russia and 11 other former Soviet republics. - Viktor Anoshkin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
